claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has a single-phase BCC structure.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has high density.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has insufficient room-temperature ductility.
Adding a minor amount of Cr to Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will induce Laves-phase precipitation.
The precipitated phase will be a Cr-rich Laves phase with a composition such as (Hf,Mo)2Cr.
The Laves phase will form a reticulated network both at grain boundaries and within the BCC matrix.
The Laves network will mitigate crack propagation by crack deflection, branching, and pinning.
Laves precipitates will impede dislocation motion and produce precipitation strengthening.
Cr addition will significantly increase yield strength and ultimate compressive strength through solid-solution and precipitation strengthening.
The Laves-containing alloy will have slightly lower total elongation than the single-phase baseline.
Despite reduced elongation, the Laves network will improve strength-ductility synergy by preventing catastrophic brittle cleavage.
Prevention of catastrophic brittle cleavage by the secondary-phase structure was observed in NbMoCrTiAl composites.
Adding Cr will slightly increase the alloy density.
The Laves phase is denser than the baseline BCC matrix and therefore contributes to the predicted density increase.
Cr addition makes the single-phase BCC Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr structure thermodynamically unstable toward phase decomposition.
Laves precipitation reduces atomic-radius misfit and elastic energy, providing a driving force for decomposition.
A Cr concentration above approximately 2-5 at.% is likely required to trigger Laves-phase precipitation.
Excessive Cr can produce a continuous brittle Laves network that causes immediate catastrophic failure.
The proposed Laves phase is stable at room temperature.
The baseline is simultaneously described as highly ductile and low-strength while also suffering from brittle cleavage because it lacks secondary crack-arresting phases.

contradictions.description: The baseline is initially characterized as having insufficient room-temperature ductility, but elsewhere it is described as highly ductile and as a high-ductility single-phase matrix. The intended relative meaning is not consistently stated.

The desired mediator is a reticulated Laves network, while the boundary condition warns that a continuous brittle network causes catastrophic failure; no morphological criterion distinguishes the beneficial network from the harmful continuous network.

The hypothesis attributes brittle cleavage to the baseline's lack of secondary phases and claims a secondary phase prevents cleavage, whereas the cited NbMoCrTiAl example contains substantial secondary ceramic phases and nevertheless exhibits cleavage without ductility.
